tables.title: Table 4: The Transformer generalizes well to English constituency parsing (Results are on Section 23 of WSJ)
notes: Results are on Section 23 of WSJ
Increased the maximum output length to input length + 300. We used a beam size of 21 and α = 0.3 for both WSJ only and the semi-supervised setting.

observations: The Transformer (4 layers) with semi-supervised training achieves WSJ 23 F1 = 92.7, outperforming all discriminative-only models listed except Dyer et al. (2016) [8] (generative, 93.3) and Luong et al. (2015) [23] (multi-task, 93.0).

The text states: 'Our results in Table 4 show that despite the lack of task-specific tuning our model performs surprisingly well, yielding better results than all previously reported models with the exception of the Recurrent Neural Network Grammar [8].'
In contrast to RNN sequence-to-sequence models [37], the Transformer outperforms the Berkeley-Parser [29] even when training only on the WSJ training set of 40K sentences.
uncertainties: The note 'increased the maximum output length to input length + 300' appears after the table but is not explicitly tied to any specific row; it applies generally to the Transformer experiments (rows 5 and 10), as stated in the following sentence.

The phrase 'with the exception of the Recurrent Neural Network Grammar [8]' refers to Dyer et al. (2016) [8], which appears twice (rows 4 and 12) with different training regimes — discriminative vs generative — but the text does not clarify which variant is being referenced as the exception.

The table lists two entries for 'Transformer (4 layers)' (rows 5 and 10) differing only in Training type; no further distinguishing metadata (e.g., hyperparameters, dropout, layer size) is provided in the table itself.
